lawyer:
Md Mostafa, Advocate — For the Appellants.

parties:
President, Magura Town Hall & another ------ Appellant
vs
President, Magura District Ainjibi Samity and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that, respondent No. 1 as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Magura being Title Suit No. 2 of 1999, praying for declaration of title in the suit property and for recovery of Khas possession therein. After filing the suit the plaintiff filed an application praying for temporary injunction under Order 39 rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure restraining the defendants from making any act of reconstruction or further constructions in the suit property or from in any way changing the nature and character thereof till the disposal of the suit. The plaintiff''s case, in short, is that the Magura Bar Association by organizing an amateur Dramatic Club founded Magura Theatre in 1918 for fostering cultural activities in the locality. It has been alleged that Mr Charu Chandra Sen, the Secretary of the plaintiff Samity, was the founding secretary of the Magura Theatre and it was so recorded in his name in CS Khatian No. 377 and SA Khatian No. 386. It has also been alleged that for convenience of management the plaintiff Samity subsequently made over the Magura Theatre to defendant Magura Town Club for running the same under the control and supervision of the plaintiff. It has been also alleged that it was settled between the parties that defendant Magura Town Hall would rebuild an auditorium at its own cost on the plan approved by the plaintiff. It has been further contended that long since the plaintiff Samity has been deputing at least two of its members to the Executive Committee of the Magura Town Club for looking after the interests of the plaintiff Samity. It has also been alleged that the plaintiff Samity leased out the suit property to the Magura Talkie, The Modhumita Cinema Hall and other establishments as licensees under the plaintiff and it has been realising rent from the tenants. It has been further alleged that as the Magura Town Club and its Auditorium became old and dilapidated and ultimately it was decided in February, 1998 that the Magura Town Hall Auditorium would be pulled down for the purpose of reconstruction and development on the plan approved by the plaintiff Samity and the construction works would be carried out under the direct supervision and control of the Samity, and a contractor was engaged for the purpose. At this stage the defendant illegally claimed the suit property and the suit and prayer for temporary injunction.
